description: Read logs from one or more local containers or a single remote container.

categories.name: Arguments
categories.description: Log lines, time filters and container labels.

options.detail: A container removed on exit with --rm can lose its log file before Podman reads the last lines. This also applies if another process removes the container. Also spelled -f.
A container removed on exit with --rm can lose its log file before Podman reads the last lines. This also applies if another process removes the container. Alias for --follow.

options.summary: Show a timestamp on each log line
options.detail: Adds the recorded time to each line. Use --since or --until to select a time window. Also spelled -t.

options.summary: Show the last N log lines

platform.reason: This parameter definition does not select an operating system; platform availability is not asserted

forms.grammar: Integer line count; -1 is the all-lines sentinel

options.detail: Use an integer line count. The default, -1, shows all lines. Use --tail=-1 for all lines or --tail 0 with --follow for new output only.

options.summary: Show logs starting at a time

platform.reason: This parameter definition does not select an operating system; platform availability is not asserted

forms.grammar: Unix timestamp in seconds, not milliseconds
Use a documented date/time form; quote values containing spaces
A positive Go duration counts backward from the client clock.

when_absent.meaning: No explicit lower log-time cutoff is added

variants.time_basis: Unix timestamps count seconds from the epoch. Dates without a zone use UTC. Relative durations use the client clock.

options.detail: Use Unix seconds, a date such as 2026-01-01, or an RFC3339 timestamp. Use --since 10m to start ten minutes before the client’s current time. A negative duration, as in --since=-10m, starts ten minutes in the future. Calendar times without a zone use UTC.

options.summary: Show logs up to a cutoff time

forms.grammar: Unix timestamp in seconds, not milliseconds
Use a documented date/time form; quote values containing spaces
A positive Go duration counts forward from the client clock.

when_absent.meaning: No explicit upper log-time cutoff is added

variants.time_basis: Unix timestamps count seconds from the epoch. Dates without a zone use UTC. Relative durations use the client clock.

options.detail: Give a Unix time in seconds, a date, or an RFC3339 timestamp. Use --until 10m to set a cutoff ten minutes after the client’s current time. Use --until=-10m for ten minutes ago. Calendar times without a zone use UTC.
Uses each container’s name in place of its ID in the log prefix. The command podman logs -n web db prefixes local output by container name. Remote clients accept a single container. Also spelled -n.

options.summary: Give each container a different log color
options.detail: Color distinguishes sources when reading several local containers. A remote client accepts one container per invocation.
